answer.rationale: Rollback is unavailable: the in-window release is a non-revertible security patch, so memory_b1 is not actionable. Symptom is write-path p99 at 5x under daily-peak settlement writes; objective is sustained availability without dropping customer writes. That rules out enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4 fail-fast can shed writes) and makes regional failover unattractive until cutover risk to in-flight settlements is better known. Remaining levers are add_capacity (memory_b3 headroom kept queues flat under surge) versus route_read_replicas (memory_b5 offloaded reads and write latency recovered). Stated load is heavy writes, not report/dashboard read contention, so capacity is the better current fit—but b3 was provisioning before a peak, not mid-peak, and b5 is the only inherited case that directly recovered transactional write latency, so those two archives need checking before commit. Scale stays a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout because cause (patch cost vs pure write surge vs hidden read mix) is still uncertain.
